candidates.text: Hypothesis: a real multiline private-key block survives because the PEM regex expects literal backslash-n separators and only a generic header. Applicability: the central formatter is attached to file logging, and the analyst may call it directly on a disposable string. Bounded test: emit generic, RSA, and ENCRYPTED blocks with real newlines and a base64 marker, plus a literal-backslash-n control. Expected result: base64 markers disappear and END headers remain; falsifier: any marker survives. Cleanup: delete the temporary log and fixture key material.

Hypothesis: short numeric authentication codes pass through because no masker targets passcode, auth_code, mfa_code, or otp keys, and the connection-token value floor is longer than six digits. Applicability: an authentication path logs a request-data mapping after omitting only a password field. Bounded test: emit passcode=482913 and quoted PASSCODE/auth_code/mfa_code variants alongside an unrelated six-digit latency value. Expected result: code values become masked and the latency value is unchanged; falsifier: a code survives or the unrelated number is altered. Cleanup: delete the temporary log.

Hypothesis: a short signed-URL signature and an authorization-scheme credential survive because the signed-URL matcher requires a longer value and no matcher recognizes the authorization-scheme keyword. Applicability: third-party SDK loggers share the formatter and may print request headers or URLs. Bounded test: emit a short sig= value, a long sig= control, and an authorization header carrying a marker token. Expected result: short and long signatures and the header credential are masked; falsifier: any marker survives while its control is masked. Cleanup: delete fixture URLs and logs.

Hypothesis: mixed-case or nested JSON secret keys evade exact-name regexes. Applicability: structured dictionaries are logged as repr or JSON strings. Bounded test: emit private-key-data, auth-token, and cloud-key keys with mixed case and nesting. Expected result: all variants mask identically to lowercase baselines; falsifier: a mixed-case key leaks. Note: several existing patterns already compile case-insensitively, so the hypothesis may only hold for key names absent from the list. Cleanup: delete fixture dictionaries and logs.

Hypothesis: a repair that closes format gaps can still over-mask benign fields or leave a gap partially visible. Applicability: a candidate patch is applied only to the disposable local copy. Bounded test: run existing unit-test vectors plus benign six-digit numbers, public-certificate text, and already-masked token/password values through pristine and patched formatters. Expected result: all demonstrated secrets mask and benign text stays byte-identical; falsifier: benign-only input changes beyond the intended secret fields or a demonstrated secret still leaks. Cleanup: remove both temporary trees.
